parts.title: Pallavi
text: O leader of the pramada ganas, you are the color of vermillion and the ocean of compassion. You have the visage of the mighty elephant and a protruding belly. You hold goddess lakshmi in your hand. O son of Parvathi, you are worshipped by the gods.

parts.title: Charanam 1
text: You have all the holy men at your feet, and you are worshipped by the pramadha ganas, who are the followers of lord Siva. You grant your devotees all their wishes, and I bow to you.

parts.title: Charanam 2
text: You are the first to receive obeisance when one sets out to acquire any kind of knowledge. You are the greatest of all, and I pray to you.

words.title: Pallavi
lyric: Sri Gananatha sindhoora varna karuNa saagara kari vadana
lambodara lakumi-karaa ambaa suta amara vinutha
text: O leader of the pramada ganas (“sri gana natha”), you are the color of vermillion (“sindhura varna”) and the ocean of compassion (“karuna sagara”). You have the visage (“vadana”) of the mighty elephant (“kari”) and a protruding belly (“lambodara”). You hold goddess lakshmi (“lakumi”) in your hand (“kara”). O son of Parvathi (“amba sutha”), you are worshipped by (“vinutha”) the gods (“amara”).

words.title: Charanam 1
lyric: siddha chaaraNa gaNa sEvita siddhi vinayaka tE namo namo
text: You have all the holy men at your feet (“siddha charana”), and you are worshipped by the pramadha ganas, who are the followers of lord Siva (“gaNa sEvitha”).
You grant your devotees all their wishes (“siddhi vinAyaka”), and I bow to you (“tE namo”).

words.title: Charanam 2
lyric: sakala vidya aadi poojitha sarvothama tE namo namo
text: You are the first (“aadi”) to receive obeisance (“poojitha”) when one sets out to acquire any kind of knowledge (“sakala vidhya”).
You are the greatest of all (“sarvothama”), and I pray to you.

parts.title: Pallavi
text: Oh Lord of Gowri, you are as white as the jasmine flower. You wear a kreeda that looks like a palace. You spread the smell of the honey of the parijatha.

parts.title: Charanam 1
text: You sit in the golden chair. You have three eyes, and you are full of mercy.

parts.title: Charanam 2
text: Your makuta is the place of residence of the Moon and the Ganga.

words.title: Pallavi
lyric: kunda goura gowrI vara mandirAya mana makuTa mandAra kusumAkara magarandam vAsituva
text: Oh Lord of Gowri (Gowri vara mandhiraya), you are as white as the jasmine flower (Kuntha goura). You wear a kreeda that looks like a palace. You spread the smell (vasithuva) of the honey (magarantham) of the parijatha.

words.title: Charanam 1
text: Oh Lord! You have Meru Mountain as your throne (He makuta simhasana); you are the one with the third eye (virupAksha); you are merciful (karunakara) in mind and heart.

words.title: Charanam 2
lyric: chanda mAma mandAkini mandiraya mana makuTa (man)
text: Oh Lord! The Moon and the Ganges (chanda mAma mandAkini) decorate your head as a kreeda (mana makuta) that resembles a residing place (mandiraya).

parts.title: Pallavi
text: In this geetham, Purandaradasa describes the attributes of the devotees of the god Hari.
Look! The followers of Hari scoop water from the lake and pour it back into the lake while worshipping, with the intention of obtaining boons from the god.
In a similar manner, the life given as a considerate bequest by Hari is surrendered back to him.

parts.title: Charanam
text: These holy men spend their lives feasting their eyes on the lotus feet of the god who is the master of Purandara dasa.

words.title: Pallavi
lyric: kereya neeranu kerege jalli varava paDedava ranti kanero!
hariya karuNadoLaada BhAgyava hari samaarpane maaDi bradukero
text: The followers of Hari scoop water (“neeranu”) from the lake (“kere”) and pour (“jalli”) it back into the lake (“kere ge”) while worshipping, with the intention of obtaining boons (“varava padeda rante”) from the god. Look (“kanero”)!
In a similar manner, the life given as a considerate bequest (“karunadoLaada bhagyavu”) by Hari (“hari ya”) is (“maadi”) surrendered back to him (“hari samarpana”).

words.title: Charanam
lyric: Sree purandara viThala rAyA charaNa kamalava nodi bradukero
text: These holy men spend their lives (“bradukeru”) feasting their eyes (“nodi”) on the lotus feet (“charaNa kamalava”) of the god who is the master of Purandara dasa (sri purandara viThala rAyA). The life given as a considerate bequest (“karuNadolaada bhagyavu”) by Hari (“hari ya”) is (“maadi”) surrendered back to him (“hari samarpana”).

parts.title: Pallavi
text: In this geetham, Purandara dasa describes the various names by which the god Vishnu is called.

I pray to thee, who has a lotus in his navel, the greatest of men, the personification of the eternal flame of life, the destroyer of adversity, whose stories are illustrations of purity, and who is perched on the prodigious bird Garuda.

parts.title: Anupallavi
text: He dwells in the mighty ocean, reposes on the powerful serpent Aadiseshu, is capable of miracles greater than the greatest, and is the greatest of the yadava race, Krishna. As Rama, he protected the yagnya of the great maharshi Vishwamitra, and he also preached the importance of obeying the command of his parent, Dasaratha.

parts.title: Charanam
text: I worship thee, the custodian of Vibhishana, the pious brother of the demon king Ravana. I praise thee, who bestows everything on his followers. He endows all good fortunes and fulfils all sanguine aspirations. He is our noble king, he engages our spirit with cheerfulness, and he is Rama, the lord of Purandara dasa.

words.title: Pallavi
lyric: Padumanaabha Parama Purushaa Param Jyoti Swaroopaa
Vidhura Vandya Vimala Charita Vihanga Adirohana
text: I pray to thee, who has a lotus in his navel (“paduma nabha”), the greatest of men (“parama purusha”), the personification of the eternal flame (“paramjyothi swarupa”) of life, the destroyer (“vandhya”) of adversity (“vidhura”), whose stories (“charitha”) are illustrations of purity (“vimala”), and who is perched (“adhirohana”) on the prodigious bird Garuda (“vihanga”).

words.title: Anu Pallavi
lyric: Udadhi Nivaasa Uraga Shayana Unnatonnata Mahima
Yadukulottama Yagnya Rakshaka Yagnya Shikshaka Raama Naama
text: He dwells (“nivasa”) in the mighty ocean (“udhadhi”), reposes (“sayana”) on the powerful serpent Aadiseshu (“uraga”), is capable of miracles (“mahima”) greater than the greatest (“unnathonnatha”), and is the greatest of the yadava race (“yadukulothama”), Krishna. As Rama, he protected (“rakshaka”) the yagnya of the great maharshi Vishwamitra, and he also preached (“sikshaka”) the importance of obeying the command (“Agnya”) of his parent, Dasaratha.

words.title: Charanam
lyric: Vibheeshana Paalaka Namo Namo Ibha Varadaayaka Namo Namo
Shubha Prada Sumanorada Surendra Manoranjanaa Abhinava
text: I worship thee (“namo namo”), the custodian (“paalaka”) of Vibhishana, the pious brother of the demon king Ravana. I praise thee (“namo namo”), who bestows (“vara daayaka”) everything on his followers (“vibhow”). He endows all good fortunes (“subha prada”) and fulfils all sanguine aspirations (“su manorathaya”). He is our noble king (“su-rendra”), he engages our spirit (“abhinava”) with cheerfulness (“mano ranjana”), and he is Rama, the lord (“bhallare”) of Purandara dasa.
This geetham by purandara vittalaraya describes the way lord Venkataachala showers his grace on his devotees.
Who can ride one's own unsteady and wavering mind but the Lord Venkataachala, who is known to vanquish fear in his devotees' hearts?
This geetham by purandara vittalaraya describes the way lord Venkataachala showers his grace on his devotees.

Who can ride (sevare) one's own unsteady and wavering mind (keralda manadani) but the Lord Venkataachala (deva shree vEnkaTAchala), who is known to vanquish fear (Bhayasamaya) in his devotees' hearts?
In this geetham, Sri Purandara dasu compares human life with the leakage of water from a pot.

I wasted much of the time in my life by not listening to, or not having awareness of, great descriptions of ancient texts and scriptures, just as we watch water get away through the outlet under the pot. Going forward, I will fill my heart with you, the Sarvaantaryami, and keep it pure.

lyric: dhEnnam Taala dhEnnam Taala parigatu rE rE
text: I wasted (parigatu) much of the time (Taala) in my life by not listening to, or not having awareness (dhEnnam) of, great descriptions of ancient texts and scriptures (Shaastrapurana), just as we watch (AnalEkara) water (unni) get away through the outlet (pOladi) under the pot. Going forward, I (naM) will fill my heart with you (parigatam), the Sarvaantaryami, and keep it pure.

Oh Rama, you are decorated by the kumkum that is Sita, the daughter of Janaka. You are the one who killed emperor Bali. You have Garuda as your vahana. You saved Gajendra and granted him boons. You are the lord of the auspicious Lakshmi. You reside in Karigiri.

Oh Rama, you are decorated by the kumkum (“kuca kumkuma”) that is Sita, the daughter of Janaka (“Janaka sutha”). You are the one who killed emperor Bali (“Baliharure”). You have Garuda as your vahana (“khaga vahana”). You saved Gajendra and granted him boons (“karivarada”). You are the lord (“manoharure”) of the auspicious (“kalyana”) Lakshmi (“Perundevi”). You reside (“nivasure”) in Karigiri.

Shree Raamachandra is like the Paarijaatha tree to all his devotees. He pleases one and all with his divine qualities. He is like the bee that flies over the lotus of Sita's face. May he grant benediction (i.e. bless us) forever.

lyric: kaLyANa guNAbhi rAma sItA mukha ambOruha
text: Shree Raamachandra is like the pArijAta (wish-fulfilling) tree to all (“samasta”) his devotees (“asritha”). He pleases one and all with his divine (“kaLyANa”) qualities (“guNa”). He is like the bee (“sancharIka”) that flies over the lotus (“amboruha”) of Sita's face (“mukha”). May He grant (“maata notu”) benediction (i.e. bless us) [“mangaLa”] forever (“nirantaram”).

You whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus, who roam about in the pure water like a queen of swans, whose hips are like a lion's, who shower brightness like the Sun and the moon, whose fragrant bindi (tilakam) is combined with both Chandan and Kumkum, who have thick hair, who walk like the queen of swans among bunches of lotuses: O Goddess!! Shower your blessings on me.

lyric: jaaji Sayya kacha kucha ghana jaga-
text: You whose eyes are like the petals of a lotus (kamala suLOchana), who roam about in the pure water (vimala taTaakini) like a queen of swans (maraaLa gaamini), whose hips (madhyae) are like a lion's (kari hara), who shower brightness (bimbaanana) like the Sun and the moon (vidhu manDalare), whose fragrant (parimaLa) bindi (tilakam) is combined (samkalita) with both Chandan and Kumkum, who have thick hair (kacha kucha), who walk like the queen of swans (maraaLa gaamini) among bunches of lotuses (ambhOja): O Goddess!! Shower your blessings on me.

You hold the divine veena in your soft hands. You are the queen of the omniscient. Your eyes are like lotus petals. Your curly tresses resemble bees. The Devas worship your auspicious form. You have unequaled virtuous qualities. You give endless victory. You are Ranganaayaki, the consort of Ranganatha. You grant the boons desired by your devotees. O Mother of Brahma, who is seated on a lotus! Victory to you.

lyric: varaveeNA mRdu pAni vanaruha lOchana raaNi
nirupama Subha guNa lOla niratajaya prada Seela
saraseejasana jananI jaya jaya jaya jaya vANI
text: You hold the divine (“vara”) veena in your soft (“mrudu”) hands (“paani”). You are the queen (“raani”) of the omniscient. Your eyes (“lochana”) are like lotus petals (“vanaruha”). Your curly (“suruchira”) tresses (“veni”) resemble bees (“bambhara”). The Devas (“Sura”) worship (“nuta”) your auspicious form (“kalyaani”). You have (“lola”) unequaled (“nir-upama”) virtuous (“shuba”) qualities (“guna”). You (“sheela”) give (“prada”) endless (“narathi”) victory (“jaya”). You are Ranganaayaki, the consort (“priya”) of Ranganatha (“varadaa”). You grant (“daayaki”) the boons (“phala”) desired (“vaanchita”) by your devotees. O Mother (“janani”) of Brahma, who is seated on a lotus (“saraseeja-asana”)! Victory (“jaya”) to you.
In this geetam, the author describes a part of the KurmaPuranam about the nobleness of maha Vishnu.

In Koormavatara, He is the one who bore the whole Mandara Parvata on His back, who killed the Rakshasa Mura, who killed the Danavas (evil), who wore a peacock feather on His crown, and who has auspicious marks on His feet. O Krishna!! Grant us Moksha.

He is the one who bore the whole Mandara Parvata (mandara dhaarae) on His back, who killed the Rakshasa Mura (mOkshamu raarae), who killed the Danavas (evil) (daitya kulaantaka), who is pure (paavana moortae), who wore a peacock feather (mayoora) on His crown (makuTa), and who has auspicious marks (Subharaekha) on His feet (pada).

O Govinda!! You who are endless, O Vishnu, who killed the Raakshasa Madhu, who wear the tulasi mala, who hold Garuda on your flag, who killed the demon Muku, who hold SriDevi in your heart. O benevolent king of Raghuvamsha, brother of Balarama, O Rama, victory to you, who are dearest to Sita, who are crowned as King of Ayodhya: shower your blessings on me.

O Govinda (gOvinda)!! You who are endless (achyuta), O Vishnu (harae), who killed the Raakshasa Madhu (madhusoodhana), who wear the tulasi garland (vanamaala), who hold Garuda on your flag (garuDha dhvaja), who killed the demon Muku (mukunda), who hold SriDevi (Goddess Lakshmi) in your heart (Sreedhara). O benevolent king of Raghuvamsha (Sree raghupatae), brother of Balarama (sankarshaNa), O beautiful Rama, victory to you (sundaraanga jayajaya), who are dearest to Sita (seetaabhiraama), who are crowned as King of Ayodhya (paTTaabhiraama): shower your blessings (pahi) on me (maam).
O goddess saraswati, shower your blessings, stay on my tongue and bless me with sweet, easy words to take birth from my mouth, the same way as for sage Valmiki, who wrote the Ramayana.

lyric: DiMdada nanna mukhadali maadhurya Sree lAlita vachanagaLu
janisuvEkE yaavalanugraha varadi vAlmIki muni veldanu
text: O goddess saraswati (saraswati), shower (Dindada) your blessings (yaavalanugraha), stay (kuNisali) on my tongue (nanna naaligeyali) and bless (yaavalanugraha varadi) me with sweet, easy (maadhurya lalita) words (vachanagaLu) to take birth (janisuvEkE) from my mouth (nanna mukhadali), the same way (veldanu) as for sage Valmiki (vAlmIki muni), who wrote the Ramayana (Sree ramaNa Subha charitraM).

Oh merciful one, with lotus-like eyes! You are an ocean of mercy, and you showed kindness to the elephant king, Gajendra. You, the lord of Lakshmi, slew the demons Keshi and Narakaasura. You are so kind at the time of protecting the king of the Devas (Indra).

lyric: kamalajAdaLa vimala su-nayana kari varada karuNAmbudhE
kEshi narakAsura vibhEdana varada vELa sura purOttama
text: Oh merciful one, with lotus-like (“kamalajadala”) eyes (“vimala su-nayana”)! You are an ocean (“ambudhe”) of mercy (“karuNa”), and you showed (“Saradhe”) kindness (“varada”) to the elephant king (“kari”), Gajendra. You, the lord (“kaanthaa”) of Lakshmi (“kamaLaa”), slew (“vibhedana”) the demons (“asura”) Keshi and Narakaasura. You are so kind at the time (vELa) of protecting (varada) the king of the Devas (sura purOttama).
O Goddess! The appearance of your bridal hair resembles a thick bunch of bees over the lotus. O Goddess gowrI, with your lotus-like feet, remove our sins.

O Goddess (amarI)! The appearance (mukarI – kRtaM) of your bridal hair (kabarI) resembles a thick bunch of bees (bhara bhramarI) over the lotus. O Goddess gowrI (gourI), with your (tava) lotus-like feet (charaNa pankajaM), remove (dUrI karOtu) our (mama) sins (duritaM).

O Lord! Shree Raamachandra of Ayodhya, you are like a swan in the hearts of all devotees, and you are the ruler and bearer of all lokas. You fulfilled Dasharadh's wish, and you were good fortune to Kausalya in being her son. I, Gurumurti, bow to your feet and praise you, that you may shower your grace and give me a thought of a beautiful song, with a mixture of good idioms and incomparable phrases to praise you. Hey Lord! Protect me.

lyric: shrI rAmacandra sAkEtapuravAsA munijana mAnasa hamsa nikhila lOka pAlana
dhuriNa kausalyAbhAgya rUpa dashAradE purayamE vAncAm tava vandE
pAda kamala maNI sankrpalO gAna phaNitima kalaya mudamatulam dEhi mE
bhO svAmin pAlaya mAm gurumUrti nAmakam
text: O Lord! Shree Raamachandra of Ayodhya (sAkEtapuravAsA), you are like a swan (hamsa) in the hearts (mAnasa) of all devotees (munijana), and you are the ruler (pAlana) and bearer (dhuriNa) of all lokas (nikhila lOka). You fulfilled (pura yamE) Dasharadh's (dashAradE) wish (vAncAm), and you were good fortune (bhAgyarUpa) to Kausalya in being her son. I, Gurumurti, bow my body (manisha) to your (tava) lotus-like (kamala) feet (pAda) and praise you (vandE), that you may shower your grace and give (dEhi) me (mE) a thought of a beautiful (amudam) song (gAna), with a mixture (kalaya) of good idioms (phaNiti) and incomparable phrases (atulam) to praise you. Hey Lord! Protect me.
O Sri Ramachandra! You are the beacon of the solar dynasty!
You watch over the devas!
You take care of ordinary mortals!
You give pleasure to Seetha!
You are the brave one!
You have vanquished Ravana!
You fulfill the desires of your devotees!
Lord, please protect me.

lyric: rE rE SrI rAmachandrA raghuvamSa tilakA rAghavEndrA
Sritajana pOshakurE! sItA manOranjana rE rE dheerA!
[Aa iya iya! Aa iya iya! Aa iya rE!]
text: O (“rere”) Sri Ramachandra! You are the beacon (“tilakaa”) of the solar (“raghu”) dynasty (“vamsha”)!
You watch over the devas (“rAghavEndrA”)!
You take care of (“pOshakure”) ordinary mortals (“Srita-jana”)!
You give pleasure (“manoranjana”) to Seetha!
You are the brave one (“dhIrA”)!
You have vanquished (“antakurE”) Ravana!
You fulfill the desires (“mandhAra”) of your devotees (“dhIna jana”)!
Lord, please protect me (“mAmava”).
[Aa iya iya! Aa iya iya! Aa iya rE!] – This phrase has no meaning. Such phrases are used to set the lines to the tAla.

You have eyes like the fish. May there be auspiciousness. You have eyes that fulfill the desires of devotees. Your eyes are enchanting. You are the best among the matchless. Your speech accompanies omkar and is very sweetly decorated.

You have fearful long hands capable of killing the war-loving madhu and kaitaba. You are the mother of elephant-faced vinayaka and Subramanya. May there be auspiciousness. Kathyayini, hey kali! rudhra priya! You have a sweet voice like that of the veena. Your nails shine like lightning on your body, which looks like clouds.
You are the mistress of Lord Sokkanatha, who stays in Madurapuri.

lyric: mInAkshi jaya kAmAkshi — kankatIka vAmAkshi — appratibha prabha vOnnata — madhura madhura sAlamkArA — OmkArA kalitA lApa — yuddha mitra madhu kaitapa — khanDa ChanDa danDanu jAnu (mInAkshi jaya)
madayA vala yAna kArtikEya jananI rE rE — kAtyAyani kALi rudrAni — vINA nigvANI kAranakara - nakha Sikharam — jaya madhurAbham prANa jIvure - SokkanAda swAmy -jIvure

text: O sweetest one, who respects Goddess Parvati's husband. Krishna! I praise you. You have eyes as bright as the lotus. You are simply modest in appearance, the one who grants boons to the entire world. You are so auspicious among all kings, and you destroyed demons like madhu. You made Goddess Lakshmi happy by letting her reside in your heart. You wore everlasting ornaments in the shape of a serpent. You pursued the greatest degree of virtue. You rest on the Serpent. Release me from attachments and emotions and give me salvation.

lyric: maNi rAja kunDalaM madhu daitya khanDanaM
text: O sweetest one (mAdhava), who respects (mAnIta) Goddess Parvati's (uma) husband (dhavam). Krishna (mAdhavaM), I praise you (vandE). You have eyes as bright (lOchanaM) as the lotus (pankaja). Release (mOchanaM) me from attachments (bandha) and emotions (bhava). You appear as if you wore clouds (neerabha) as clothes (vasnaM), and you are the one who can bless the entire world (nikhila) with the one (eka) of many boons (daayinaM), i.e., moksha. You are so auspicious (like maNi) among all rAjas (rAja kunDalaM). You destroyed (khanDanaM) demons (daitya) like madhu. You made Goddess Lakshmi (indira) happy (ullAsa) by letting her reside in your heart (vaksha). You wore everlasting (nava) ornaments (kunDalam) in the shape of a serpent (nAga). You pursued (manDalam) the greatest degree (Arya) of virtue (guNa). You rest on the Serpent, and you give (dAyinaM) salvation (mOksha) to your devotees (ASrita).

O victorious Lord Vishnu! You are an ocean of mercy. Your lotus-like feet are incomparable. You are the husband of Goddess Lakshmi. I meditate on your feet, which care for and satisfy the devotees' wishes.

This raagam dhanyaasi is of a kind that is pleasant to hear and sing. It is derived from the 8th MeLakarta raga Hanumattodi, with 5 swaras while ascending, leaving out the 2 swaras 'R' and 'D', and all swaras while descending. The swaras 'G' and 'D' (gadha) sound splendid in this raga. This raga is played in all the stayi levels and offers different pleasures of sound. This is one of the writings of the great gurumoorty.

lyric: dhanyAsi rAgaM gAya SruNuta lakshaNaM akhilaM
ArOhaeridha tyaktaM avarOha pUrNaM mandhra madhya
tAra kalitaM gadha lasitaM nAda bhEda dhurINa gurumUrtE prasIda
text: O victorious (jaya) Lord Vishnu! You are an ocean (sindhO) of mercy (karuNaa). Your (tava) lotus (ambhujam)-like feet (pAdAm) are incomparable (atulam). O husband of Goddess Lakshmi (Sreekaanta), I meditate (dhyaayaami) on your (tava) feet (charaNE), which care for and satisfy (aalana paalanaa) the devotees (bhakta).

This raagam dhanyaasi is of a kind (lakshaNaM) that is pleasant (akhilaM) to hear (sruNuta) and sing (gaaya). It is derived (janyaM) from the 8th MeLakarta (ashTamaadhikaari) raga Hanumattodi, with 5 (auDava) swaras while ascending (aarOhae), leaving out (tyaktaM) 2 swaras ('R', 'D'), and all (sampoorNa) swaras while descending (avarOha). The swaras 'G' and 'D' (gadha) sound splendid in this raga. This raga is played in all the stayi levels (mandhra, Madhya, taara kalitaM) and offers different pleasures (bhEda) of sound (naada). This is one of the writings (praseeda) of the great (dhurINa) gurumoorty.

You are the one who killed the demon kamsa, the one who killed mura, the one who steals the hearts of the gOpeekaas just as you steal butter. You are brilliant among the yaadavaas. You are so merciful. You destroyed narakaasura. You love playing the flute and being playful with rukmiNi and satyabhamaa. You save sages, Lord Krishna. Victory to you.

This is Sahanaa raga, derived from HarikaambhOji. It has trembling movements of the swara 'ga', a long stay on the swara 'ma', the swara 'da' that sits next to sudda daivata, and the swara 'ni' that is near to daivata. Playing the swaras gives the pleasure of listening to smooth movements between them. This is a propitiated raga, played even with zig-zag movement on all swaras. O Lord Krishna, listen to this subject-oriented raga. With your kindness, provide us with victory.

You are the one who killed the demon (asura) kamsa (kaMsa), the one who killed (arae) mura (muraa), the one who steals the hearts of the gOpeekaas (gOpeekaa jaara) just as you steal (chOra) butter (navneeta). You are brilliant (chandra) among the yaadavaas (yaadavaabdi). You are as merciful (kRpaa) as an ocean (saNdra). You destroyed (aNtaka) narakaasura (naraka). You love (priyure) playing the flute (vENunaada) and being playful (vilAsita) with rukmiNi and satyabhaamaa. You protect deities (sura sEvya); protect (pAhi) me (mAm).

This is Sahanaa raga, derived (janyaM) from HarikaambhOji. It has trembling (kaMpita) movements of the swara 'ga' (gaandharaM), a long (deergha) stay on the swara 'ma' (madhyamaM), the swara 'da' that sits next to sudda daivata (chaturSRti daivata), and the swara 'ni' that is near to daivata (kaiSiki nishaada). Playing (lasitaM) the swaras gives the pleasure of listening to smooth oscillations (kaMpita) between them. This is a propitiated raga, played even with zig-zag (vakra) movement on all (sampoorNam) swaras. O Lord Krishna (chidrUpArjunasArathE), listen (SruNu) to this subject-oriented (bhaashAnga) raga. With your kindness (kRpA LO), provide us with victory (jaya).
The flavour of ragam Arabhi is defined by its structure.

In ascending order the notes 'ga' and 'ni' are absent, and in descending order all seven swaras are present, hence auDava saMpUrNaM. It is derived from the parent ragam SaMkarAbharaNa. While doing alapana, phrases with the support of the notes 'da' and 'ni' can be used as nyasa. O fortunate people, listen to the ragam named Arabhi.

In all Sastras and puranas, this raga is significant to sing. This geetam has significant notes to emphasize the raga bhava, and it was composed by paidala gurumurti, who is versed in the scientific knowledge of raga.
The flavour (lakshaNaM) of ragam (rAga) Arabhi is defined by its structure (vachmi).

In ascending (ArOhE) order the notes 'ga' and 'ni' are absent (gAndhAra nishAda rahitaM), and in descending (avarOhE) order all seven swaras are present (pUrNaM), hence auDava saMpUrNaM (5-7). It is derived from the parent (janyaM) ragam SaMkarAbharaNa. While doing alapana (tAnaM), phrases with the support of the notes 'da' and 'ni' can be used as nyasa (tEshu dhaivata nishAdasahitaM nyAsaM). O fortunate people (saMto), listen (Akalayantu) to the ragam named (nAmakam) Arabhi.

In all Sastras and puranas (sarvataM trEshu), this raga is significant (kuSalAvAdi) to sing (gAnavEttArO). This geetam has significant notes (saMvAdyanuvAdi vivAdikalita) to emphasize the raga bhava, and it was composed (virachitamimaM) by paidala gurumurti (paiDAlAnvayAlankAra gurumUrti), who is versed in the scientific knowledge of raga (SAstrajna).
In this gItam, Sri Paidalagurumoorti sastri explains the greatness of his guru Venkata subbayya.

Sri Venkata subbayya, who belongs to the chinakota dynasty, is a well-known guru of sangeetam. You have blessed your disciples with the sagacious ability to write gIta epics. You led an auspicious life with such disciples. The swara raga that took birth from you has a proven visibility of difference in swara vibrance. Victory to you!

This geetam is composed by Paidalagurumoorti sastri of the paidala vamsa, who is an expert in geeta sastra. It has the structure of seven swara ascending and descending notes, is suitable for singing in all 3 levels, and suits the 4 Vedic languages with no restriction. I offer this geetam to you and wish us happiness.

lyric: chinakOTa vaMSa jaladhE tAvaka charaNAbja bhaktirmEstu
gIta prabandha rachanA chAturI vilasachChishya paraMpara
vilasati vaSaMvadaM jaya jaya tE namO namO
pravINa rAgAnga chaturvidyA vistRta kalpanA chAturyAkalita
ghananaya dESya saMsthApanAchArya paiDAla vaMSa jAta
text: Sri Venkata subbayya, who belongs to the chinakota dynasty (chinakOTa vaMSa jaladhE), is well known (durandhara) for teaching sangeetam (gAnavidyA). You have blessed your disciples with the sagacious (chAturI) ability of writing (rachanA) gIta epics (gIta prabandha). You led an auspicious (virAjamAna) life with such disciples. The swara raga (sanjAtarAgasarvasvaM) that took birth (nikaTEvA) from you (tava) has proven the visibility of difference in swara vibrance (nAdabhEda). Victory to you! (jaya jaya tE)

This geetam is composed by Paidalagurumoorti sastri of the paidala vamsa (paiDAla vaMSa jAta), who is an expert (pravINa) in geeta sastra (gItaSAstra). It has the structure of seven (saptasvaragrAma) ascending and descending swara notes (mUrchanAkalita), is suitable for singing in all 3 levels (mandhra madhyamasthAnatraya), and resembles the imagination (kalpanA) in showing the sagacity (chAturyAkalita) of 4 Vedic languages (chaturvi dyA) with no restriction (nirankuSa). I offer this geetam to you and wish us happiness (mudEtEstu).

O Goddess! Daughter of himachala, you are good fortune for the devotees. You are kind to the people in all the lokas. You are a well-wisher of Lord Shiva, you shower happiness and knowledge, and we bow to you and praise you. You have beautiful eyebrows; you are an ocean of knowledge to the world. This geetam is in nata raga, which is a parent raga. This raga has sudda 'sa', shadsruti 'ri' (level 3), antara 'ga', sudda 'ma', sudda 'pa', shadsruti 'da' (level 3) and chatushadja 'ni'. Sri Gopalaraya of the kandregula dynasty praises the Goddess with this geetam.

lyric: kAnDrEgula vaMSa tilaka gOpala rAya vinutE
Suddha madhyama Suddha panchama shaDsRti daivatayuta
kAnDrEgula vaMSa tilaka gOpala rAya vinutE
text: O Goddess! Daughter of himachala, you are good fortune for the devotees. You are kind to the people in all the lokas. You are a well-wisher of Lord Shiva, you shower happiness and knowledge, and we bow to you and praise you. You have beautiful eyebrows; you are an ocean of knowledge to the world. This geetam is in nata raga, which is a parent raga. This raga has sudda 'sa', shadsruti 'ri' (level 3), antara 'ga', sudda 'ma', sudda 'pa', shadsruti 'da' (level 3) and chatushadja 'ni'. Sri Gopalaraya of the kandregula dynasty praises the Goddess with this geetam.

O Sri Rama! Son of the luckiest Kowsalya, you are the God of Grace for all your devotees and grant them all they wish for. You are always worshipped by Sita and praised by all Devathas. By worshipping you, your devotees find protection and shelter in your arms. O lotus-eyed and blue-shaded Rama, you are worshipped by Lord Brahma and the rest, and you are the treasure of all the vedas bestowed in you.

O Sri Rama! Son (rUpa) of the luckiest (bhAgya) Kowsalya, you are kind (kRpAlO) and the God of Grace (dEvadEva) for all your devotees. Show the direction (disamE) of devotion (bhaktiM) and grant (dAyaka) them all they wish (kAmita) for. You are always worshipped (kAnta) by Sita (ramA) and praised (sEvya) by all Devathas (sura). Your devotees (ASritajana) find protection (mandAra) and shelter in your arms (charaNa), worshipped (vandita) by the world (akhilalOka). O lotus-eyed (kamalAksha) and blue-shaded (nIla varNa) Rama, you are worshipped by Lord Brahma (jalajAta prabhava) and the rest (Adi), and you are the treasure (nigama) of all the vedas (vEdya) bestowed in you.

O Ruler Nageswara, you are the protector of vandis and budhas. We praise your feet, which fulfil our wishes. I sing your greatness with the transformation of music. You have the moon decorating your head. You glitter with tone, as you wear serpents as ornaments. You have a crystal body and have music as your ocean. You are splendid, having raga as waves. If we compare life to a boat, you have swaras as the ladder and sruti as the curtain; you shine by building the above qualities of sound as a periphery. O well-wisher, give us happiness.

lyric: rAga vIchiviraaja mAna kAlADi nauka madhyE
text: O Ruler (pAlaya) Nageswara (nAgESvara), you are the protector (pArijAta) of vandis and budhas (vandibudhAvali). We praise (namAmi) your (tava) feet (charaNaM), which fulfil (dhIrapi) our wishes (vAnChati). I sing (gAtum) your (tava) greatness (mahimAnam) with the transformation (vaikharyA) of music (gAna). You have the moon (chandrakaLA) decorating your head (avataMsa). You glitter (rAjita) with tone (rAga), as you wear serpents (nAga) as ornaments (abhUsha). You have a pure crystal (Sudda spaTika) body (dEha) and have music (gAna) as your ocean (samudra). You are splendid, having raga as waves (vIchi). If we compare life to a boat, you have swaras as the ladder (sOpAna) and sruti as the curtain (vAtayana); you shine (vilasita) by building the above qualities of sound (nAda) as a periphery (prAsAda). O well-wisher (SaMbhO), give (dEhi) us happiness (mudaM).

O Lord Krishna, you are the infatuator of all three lokas. With the pleasant music that you create from the flute (made of wood), you capture the hearts of all the gopikas. In the same way, eradicate our sins in this kaliyuga. Bless me with friendly speech. You who killed Kamsa, I bow to and praise your feet. Your eyes seem victorious compared with lotus petals, and they create an illusion for the bees. You have a body tone resembling the clouds; you are splendid with your indulgent, gentle smile. Save us.

lyric: bhuvanatraya mOhana vaMSa raMdhra niSitanAda bhEda
kaMsa madana namAmi tE padasarOja yugaLiM nayana
jalada paLi rAjita gAtrA ruchira mandahAsa vilasita
a iyyati yya iyyaM vayya a...
text: O Lord Krishna, you are the infatuator (mOhana) of all three lokas (bhuvanatraya). With the pleasant music (nAda bhEda) that you create (niSita) from the flute (made of wood - vaMSa raMdhra), you capture the hearts (hRchchOra) of all the gopikas (gOpavadhU). In the same way, eradicate our sins (kalushamupaSamaya) in this kaliyuga (kalimalApahArin). Bless me (vitaramE) with friendly speech (vAgvibhavaM). You who killed (madana) Kamsa (kaMsa), I bow to and praise your feet (padasarOja yugaLiM). Your eyes (nayana) seem victorious (vijita) compared with lotus petals (kuvalaya), and they create an illusion (nindita) for the bees (kachALi). You have a body tone (gAtrA) resembling the clouds (jalada paLi); you shine (vilasita) with your indulgent (ruchira), gentle smile (mandahAsa). Save us.

Sri Rama, beloved of Janaki Devi, we praise you. You are the one who teaches dhanujas to save yagnas. You feel auspicious residing in the hearts of sages. You are hypnotized by sweet music. O Rama, son of Dhasharadha, shower your blessings on us. You are the well-wisher of the entire world. O Lord! Please bless us always with your beloved bhajans.

lyric: ramachandra dASaradhE rAghava vitaramE tava kRpaM
bhajanamanisaM dhEhi bhOsvAmin A iyyaM va iyya
text: Sri Rama, beloved of Janaki Devi (jAnakI ramaNa), we praise (namO namO) you (tE). You are the one who teaches (Sikshaka) dhanujas (dhanuja) to save yagnas. You feel auspicious (rAjitaM) residing in the hearts (mAnasabja) of sages (muni). You are hypnotized (lOlupa) by sweet (mAdhurya) music. O Rama, son of Dhasharadha (dASaradhE), shower (vitaram) your blessings (kRpaM) on us (mE). You are the well-wisher of the entire world. O Lord! Please bless (dhEhi) us always (amanisaM) with your (tAvakIna) splendid (suruchiraM) bhajans (bhajan).
“a iyyati iyya” – These phrases are used to adjust to the talam and have no defined meaning.

O lord Vishnu, dear to goddess lakshmi, your actions are worshipped by deities. You are a pond of all good virtues. You wear an essence garland touching your hair and heart. You have lotus-like hands, and you vow to follow the path of truth and dharma, having a virtuous history. You have a charming look that gives happiness to the devotees. You are fortunate to have Janaki devi as your wife, who has eyes that resemble lotus petals, who is worshipped by all deities, who bears thick hair and heavy breasts, who is worshipped (nuta) by great kings on earth, and who showers happiness on the world.

lyric: SrI lOla SritapAla sEvitasura gaNa lIla
kaca kucadhara sumamAla kara sarasija paripAla
sunRta vrata sucaritra surucira Subhakara gAtra
sArasa lOcana dhAtri suranuta janaka putri
text: O lord Vishnu, dear to goddess lakshmi (SrI lOla), your actions (lIla) are praised (sEvita) by deities (sura). You are a pond of all good virtues (guNanidhA). You wear (dhara) an essence (suma) garland (mAla) touching your hair and heart (kaca kuca). You have lotus (sarasija)-like hands (kara), and you vow (vrata) to follow (paripAla) the path of truth and dharma (sunRta), having a virtuous history (sucaritra). You have a charming (surucira) look that gives happiness (Subhakara gAtra) to the devotees. You are fortunate to have Janaki devi as your wife, who bears (dhAtri) eyes (lOcana) that resemble lotus (sArasa) petals, who is worshipped (nuta) by all deities (sura), who bears (dhara) thick hair (vENi) and heavy (gurutara) breasts (kuca), who is worshipped (nuta) by great kings (naravara) on earth, and who showers happiness (kalyANi) on the world.

Goddess Saraswati, the creator of sound (vANI), who carries the veena (veeNA) and books (pustaka) in her hands (pANI), shower (phaladE) us with boons (vAnchita). You have a charming (bhAsura) look, are praised (vinutE) by deities (vAsava) and worshipped (prItE) by rajas (bhUsura) in the world, and have a virtuous history (SubhacaritE). You are dear (prItE) to the praises (nuta) of deities (sura). You are so fortunate (suruchira) that the lotus (padma) bears you. Give us happiness (mAdE) and a good reputation (khyAtE). We praise (vEDeda) you (tE).

Goddess Saraswati, the creator of sound, who carries the veena and books in her hands, shower us with boons. You have a charming look, are praised by deities and worshipped by rajas in the world, and have a virtuous history. You are dear to deities. You are so fortunate that the lotus bears you. Give us happiness and a good reputation.
This geetam describes the beauty and greatness of Lord Ganesha.

O Lord Ganesha, you are praised by lord Shiva and Vishnu and worshipped by deities. You have a short semblance and one tooth, and you shower boons for all the wishes of devotees. You have four hands, holding a noose in one hand, an elephant prod in another, and your own broken tusk in the third. You have a big belly that represents joy and prosperity.

O Lord Ganesha, you are praised (vinuta) by lord Shiva (hara) and Vishnu (hari) and worshipped (poojitu) by deities (amara). You have a short (vAmana) semblance (roopa) and one tooth (Eka danta), and you shower (dAyaka) boons (phala) for all (sakala) the wishes (siddi) of devotees. You have four (chatur) hands (bhujayA), holding a noose (pASAm) in one hand, an elephant prod (amkusa) in another, and your own broken tusk (dhIshaNu) in the third. You have a big (lamba) belly (udara) that represents joy and prosperity.
